newsitem.title: ISRAEL: TV says Tuesday start on Jewish homes in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: TV says Tuesday start on Jewish homes in Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel's state-owned Channel One television said on Monday that surveying work would begin for a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem on Tuesday.
Israel's Housing Ministry spokesman Moshe Friedman told Reuters that there had been an intention to begin surveying the land on Tuesday "but someone called me and said there's been a change."
Friedman said he might have more information later in the evening.

The television said: "Our settlement reporter...says that tomorrow surveying will begin ahead of building on Har Homa. Our reporter says that if there are no petitions (against building) filed, in two weeks the first contractor will go up to build."
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government last week approved a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem. The site is called Har Homa by Israel.

The decision sparked Palestinian outrage and international criticism. On Monday, going into talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Washington, U.S. President Bill Clinton said he wished the decision had never been taken.

"I would have preferred the decision not have been made because I don't think it builds confidence, I think it builds mistrust," Clinton told reporters at the start of his Oval Office meeting with President Arafat.

Israel's moves in Jerusalem spurred violence in September. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gunbattles after Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel near Islamic holy shrines in East Jerusalem.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised internationally, it later annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future state.

The sides are to begin final status peace talks within the coming weeks at which issues including Jerusalem's status, according to a framework interim peace deal, will be negotiated. The sides are to reach a final peace accord by 1999.
Palestinians view Israeli building in Arab East Jerusalem as preempting negotiations.
